requirements.quote: An UNSUBSCRIBE packet with no payload is a protocol violation.
requirements.condition: When an UNSUBSCRIBE packet has no payload
requirements.error_behavior: Treat it as a protocol violation.
requirements.why_checkable: An empty-payload UNSUBSCRIBE can be injected and its violation path observed.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.10.4-1]	The Topic Filters (whether they contain wildcards or not) supplied in an UNSUBSCRIBE packet MUST be compared character-by-character with the current set of Topic Filters held by the Server for the Client.
If any filter matches exactly then its owning Subscription is deleted, otherwise no additional processing occurs.
requirements.condition: For every Topic Filter in an UNSUBSCRIBE packet
requirements.required_behavior: Compare it character-by-character with the Server's current Topic Filters for that Client, including filters containing wildcards.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not expand wildcards or use nonliteral matching for unsubscription.
requirements.why_checkable: Exact and near-match filters can be submitted and selected subscriptions observed.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.10.4-1]	The Topic Filters (whether they contain wildcards or not) supplied in an UNSUBSCRIBE packet MUST be compared character-by-character with the current set of Topic Filters held by the Server for the Client.
If any filter matches exactly then its owning Subscription is deleted, otherwise no additional processing occurs.
requirements.condition: When an UNSUBSCRIBE Topic Filter exactly matches a current filter
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not leave the exactly matched Subscription active.
requirements.why_checkable: Subsequent delivery or stored subscription state can verify deletion.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.10.4-1]	The Topic Filters (whether they contain wildcards or not) supplied in an UNSUBSCRIBE packet MUST be compared character-by-character with the current set of Topic Filters held by the Server for the Client.
If any filter matches exactly then its owning Subscription is deleted, otherwise no additional processing occurs.
requirements.condition: When an UNSUBSCRIBE Topic Filter has no exact match
requirements.required_behavior: Perform no additional processing for that filter.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not delete a partially matched Subscription.
requirements.why_checkable: Near-match filters can be tested for preservation of existing subscriptions.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.10.4-2]	If a Server deletes a Subscription It MUST stop adding any new messages for delivery to the Client.
requirements.condition: After the Server deletes a Subscription
requirements.required_behavior: Stop adding new messages under it for delivery to the Client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not enqueue newly matching messages under the deleted Subscription.
requirements.why_checkable: Messages published after deletion can be compared with the Client delivery queue.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.10.4-3]	If a Server deletes a Subscription It MUST complete the delivery of any QoS 1 or QoS 2 messages which it has started to send to the Client.
requirements.condition: After Subscription deletion when a QoS 1 delivery has already started
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not abandon the in-progress exchange solely because of deletion.
requirements.why_checkable: Deletion can be triggered mid-exchange and completion observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.10.4-3]	If a Server deletes a Subscription It MUST complete the delivery of any QoS 1 or QoS 2 messages which it has started to send to the Client.
requirements.condition: After Subscription deletion when a QoS 2 delivery has already started
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not abandon the in-progress exchange solely because of deletion.
requirements.why_checkable: Deletion can be triggered mid-exchange and completion observed.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.10.4-4]	The Server MUST respond to an UNSUBSUBCRIBE request by sending an UNSUBACK packet.
The UNSUBACK Packet MUST have the same Packet Identifier as the UNSUBSCRIBE Packet.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives UNSUBSCRIBE
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or substitute the response type.
requirements.why_checkable: The request and response packet types can be observed.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-3.10.4-4]	The Server MUST respond to an UNSUBSUBCRIBE request by sending an UNSUBACK packet.
The UNSUBACK Packet MUST have the same Packet Identifier as the UNSUBSCRIBE Packet.
requirements.condition: When constructing UNSUBACK
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a different Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The request and acknowledgement identifiers can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.10.4-5]	Even where no Topic Subscriptions are deleted, the Server MUST respond with an UNSUBACK.
requirements.condition: When UNSUBSCRIBE deletes no Topic Subscription
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not suppress the response because no filter matched.
requirements.why_checkable: A nonmatching filter can be submitted and the response observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.10.4-6]	If a Server receives an UNSUBSCRIBE packet that contains multiple Topic Filters it MUST handle that packet as if it had received a sequence of multiple UNSUBSCRIBE packets, except that it sends just one UNSUBACK response.
requirements.condition: When one UNSUBSCRIBE contains multiple Topic Filters
requirements.required_behavior: Process the filters as a sequence of separate UNSUBSCRIBE requests.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not collapse them into one combined matching expression.
requirements.why_checkable: Each independently matching Subscription can be checked for deletion.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.10.4-6]	If a Server receives an UNSUBSCRIBE packet that contains multiple Topic Filters it MUST handle that packet as if it had received a sequence of multiple UNSUBSCRIBE packets, except that it sends just one UNSUBACK response.
requirements.condition: When one UNSUBSCRIBE contains multiple Topic Filters
requirements.required_behavior: Send exactly one UNSUBACK for the packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send one UNSUBACK per filter.
requirements.why_checkable: The request's filter count and response packet count can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.12.4-1]	The Server MUST send a PINGRESP Packet in response to a PINGREQ packet.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives PINGREQ
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the response.
requirements.why_checkable: PINGREQ and the response packet can be observed in sequence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.14.1-1]	The Server MUST validate that reserved bits are set to zero and disconnect the Client if they are not zero.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives DISCONNECT
requirements.required_behavior: Validate that the reserved bits are all zero.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not accept them without validation.
requirements.why_checkable: Each reserved bit can be toggled and validation behavior observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.14.1-1]	The Server MUST validate that reserved bits are set to zero and disconnect the Client if they are not zero.
requirements.condition: When a received DISCONNECT has any nonzero reserved bit
requirements.why_checkable: Invalid flag patterns can be injected and connection termination observed.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.14.4-1]	After sending a DISCONNECT Packet the Client MUST close the Network Connection.
requirements.condition: After the Client sends DISCONNECT
requirements.why_checkable: Connection termination can be observed after the outbound packet.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.14.4-2]	After sending a DISCONNECT Packet the Client MUST NOT send any more Control Packets on that Network Connection.
requirements.condition: After the Client sends DISCONNECT
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send any further Control Packet on that Network Connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The post-DISCONNECT outbound trace can be checked for silence.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.14.4-3]	On receipt of DISCONNECT the Server MUST discard any Will Message associated with the current connection without publishing it, as described in Section 3.1.2.5.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives DISCONNECT for a connection with an associated Will
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retain it for later publication.
requirements.why_checkable: Server Will state can be checked after graceful DISCONNECT.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-3.14.4-3]	On receipt of DISCONNECT the Server MUST discard any Will Message associated with the current connection without publishing it, as described in Section 3.1.2.5.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives DISCONNECT for a connection with an associated Will
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not publish the Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: Subscribers can monitor the Will Topic after graceful DISCONNECT.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.1.0-1]	The Client and Server MUST store Session state for the entire duration of the Session.
requirements.condition: For the entire duration of an MQTT Session
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must store its Session state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard required Client state while the Session continues.
requirements.why_checkable: Reconnect and in-flight exchanges can reveal whether Client state persisted.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.1.0-1]	The Client and Server MUST store Session state for the entire duration of the Session.
requirements.condition: For the entire duration of an MQTT Session
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must store its Session state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard required Server state while the Session continues.
requirements.why_checkable: Reconnect and queued/in-flight exchanges can reveal whether Server state persisted.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.1.0-2]	A Session MUST last at least as long it has an active Network Connection.
requirements.condition: While a Session has an active Network Connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not terminate it before the connection ends.
requirements.why_checkable: Session state can be inspected throughout an active connection.

MUST send a PUBLISH packet with QoS=0, DUP=0.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not initiate with another Control Packet type.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-4.3.2-1]
	In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new Application Message to publish.
MUST send a PUBLISH Packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=1, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH Packet as "unacknowledged" until it has received the corresponding PUBACK packet from the receiver.
See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
requirements.condition: Each time the QoS 1 Sender has a new Application Message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send it without an identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Each new-message PUBLISH can be checked for field presence.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-4.3.2-2]
	In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Receiver
MUST respond with a PUBACK Packet containing the Packet Identifier from the incoming PUBLISH Packet, having accepted ownership of the Application Message.
After it has sent a PUBACK Packet the Receiver MUST treat any incoming PUBLISH packet that contains the same Packet Identifier as being a new publication, irrespective of the setting of its DUP flag.
requirements.condition: When the QoS 1 Receiver accepts incoming PUBLISH
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or substitute the acknowledgement type.
requirements.why_checkable: The request and response packet types can be observed.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a different identifier.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-4.3.3-1]
	In the QoS 2 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier when it has a new Application Message to publish.
MUST send a PUBLISH packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=2, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH packet as "unacknowledged" until it has received the corresponding PUBREC packet from the receiver.
See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
MUST send a PUBREL packet when it receives a PUBREC packet from the receiver.
This PUBREL packet MUST contain the same Packet Identifier as the original PUBLISH packet.
MUST treat the PUBREL packet as "unacknowledged" until it has received the corresponding PUBCOMP packet from the receiver.
MUST NOT re-send the PUBLISH once it has sent the corresponding PUBREL packet.
requirements.condition: When the QoS 2 Sender has a new Application Message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send it without an identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The initial PUBLISH can be checked for field presence.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-4.3.3-1]
	In the QoS 2 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier when it has a new Application Message to publish.
MUST send a PUBLISH packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=2, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH packet as "unacknowledged" until it has received the corresponding PUBREC packet from the receiver.
See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
MUST send a PUBREL packet when it receives a PUBREC packet from the receiver.
This PUBREL packet MUST contain the same Packet Identifier as the original PUBLISH packet.
MUST treat the PUBREL packet as "unacknowledged" until it has received the corresponding PUBCOMP packet from the receiver.
MUST NOT re-send the PUBLISH once it has sent the corresponding PUBREL packet.
requirements.condition: When the corresponding PUBCOMP arrives
requirements.required_behavior: End the PUBREL packet's unacknowledged state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not let noncorresponding PUBCOMP acknowledge it.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet Identifiers can be varied and state transitions observed.

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not resend the original PUBLISH.
requirements.why_checkable: The outbound trace after PUBREL can be checked for prohibited PUBLISH retransmission.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-4.3.3-2]
	In the QoS 2 delivery protocol, the Receiver
MUST respond with a PUBREC containing the Packet Identifier from the incoming PUBLISH Packet, having accepted ownership of the Application Message.
Until it has received the corresponding PUBREL packet, the Receiver MUST acknowledge any subsequent PUBLISH packet with the same Packet Identifier by sending a PUBREC.
It MUST NOT cause duplicate messages to be delivered to any onward recipients in this case.
MUST respond to a PUBREL packet by sending a PUBCOMP packet containing the same Packet Identifier as the PUBREL.
After it has sent a PUBCOMP, the receiver MUST treat any subsequent PUBLISH packet that contains that Packet Identifier as being a new publication.
requirements.condition: When the QoS 2 Receiver accepts incoming PUBLISH
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or substitute the response type.
requirements.why_checkable: The request and response packet types can be observed.

requirements.quote:

MUST respond with a PUBREC containing the Packet Identifier from the incoming PUBLISH Packet, having accepted ownership of the Application Message.

It MUST NOT cause duplicate messages to be delivered to any onward recipients in this case.
MUST respond to a PUBREL packet by sending a PUBCOMP packet containing the same Packet Identifier as the PUBREL.
After it has sent a PUBCOMP, the receiver MUST treat any subsequent PUBLISH packet that contains that Packet Identifier as being a new publication.
requirements.condition: When constructing initial PUBREC
requirements.required_behavior: Copy the incoming PUBLISH Packet Identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a different identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBLISH and PUBREC identifiers can be compared.

requirements.condition: Before corresponding PUBREL arrives, when another PUBLISH with the same Packet Identifier arrives

requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not acknowledge the repeated PUBLISH with a different Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The repeated PUBLISH and resulting PUBREC Packet Identifiers can be compared; the requirement follows from the same-ID retry rule and the adjacent PUBREC correlation rule.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.4.0-1]	When a Client reconnects with CleanSession set to 0, both the Client and Server MUST re-send any unacknowledged PUBLISH Packets (where QoS > 0) and PUBREL Packets using their original Packet Identifiers.
requirements.condition: When a Client reconnects with CleanSession=0 and the Client has unacknowledged QoS>0 PUBLISH packets
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must resend every such PUBLISH packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit an unacknowledged QoS>0 PUBLISH from replay.
requirements.why_checkable: Outstanding state before disconnect and packets after reconnect can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.4.0-1]	When a Client reconnects with CleanSession set to 0, both the Client and Server MUST re-send any unacknowledged PUBLISH Packets (where QoS > 0) and PUBREL Packets using their original Packet Identifiers.
requirements.condition: When the Client resends an unacknowledged QoS>0 PUBLISH after CleanSession=0 reconnect
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not allocate a new identifier for the replay.
requirements.why_checkable: Pre-disconnect and replayed PUBLISH identifiers can be compared.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-4.5.0-1]	When a Server takes ownership of an incoming Application Message it MUST add it to the Session state of those clients that have matching Subscriptions.
Matching rules are defined in Section 4.7.
requirements.condition: When the Server takes ownership of an incoming Application Message
requirements.required_behavior: Add it to the Session state of every Client with a matching Subscription.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit a Client whose Subscription matches under Section 4.7.
requirements.why_checkable: Known subscriptions and each Client's Session state can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.5.0-2]	The Client MUST acknowledge any Publish Packet it receives according to the applicable QoS rules regardless of whether it elects to process the Application Message that it contains.
requirements.condition: When the Client receives PUBLISH requiring acknowledgement
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge it according to its QoS rules.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use the wrong acknowledgement flow.
requirements.why_checkable: The incoming QoS and outbound acknowledgement can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.5.0-2]	The Client MUST acknowledge any Publish Packet it receives according to the applicable QoS rules regardless of whether it elects to process the Application Message that it contains.
requirements.condition: When the Client elects not to process the Application Message in a received PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Still perform the acknowledgement required by QoS.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not withhold acknowledgement because application processing was skipped.
requirements.why_checkable: Application rejection can be induced while observing protocol acknowledgement.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.6.0-1]	When it re-sends any PUBLISH packets, it MUST re-send them in the order in which the original PUBLISH packets were sent (this applies to QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages).
requirements.condition: When resending multiple QoS 1 PUBLISH packets
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder the retransmissions.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmission sequences can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.6.0-1]	When it re-sends any PUBLISH packets, it MUST re-send them in the order in which the original PUBLISH packets were sent (this applies to QoS 1 and QoS 2 messages).
requirements.condition: When resending multiple QoS 2 PUBLISH packets
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder the retransmissions.
requirements.why_checkable: Original and retransmission sequences can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.6.0-2]	Client MUST send PUBACK packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBLISH packets were received (QoS 1 messages).
requirements.condition: When the Client acknowledges multiple QoS 1 PUBLISH packets
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBACK packets in corresponding PUBLISH receive order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder PUBACK responses.
requirements.why_checkable: Incoming PUBLISH and outgoing PUBACK identifier sequences can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.6.0-3]	Client MUST send PUBREC packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBLISH packets were received (QoS 2 messages).
requirements.condition: When the Client acknowledges multiple QoS 2 PUBLISH packets
requirements.required_behavior: Send PUBREC packets in corresponding PUBLISH receive order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder PUBREC responses.
requirements.why_checkable: Incoming PUBLISH and outgoing PUBREC identifier sequences can be compared.

requirements.quote: [MQTT-4.6.0-4]	Client MUST send PUBREL packets in the order in which the corresponding PUBREC packets were received (QoS 2 messages).
requirements.condition: When the Client sends multiple QoS 2 PUBREL packets
requirements.required_behavior: Send them in corresponding PUBREC receive order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder PUBREL responses.
requirements.why_checkable: Incoming PUBREC and outgoing PUBREL identifier sequences can be compared.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-4.6.0-5]	A Server MUST by default treat each Topic as an "Ordered Topic".
It MAY provide an administrative or other mechanism to allow one or more Topics to be treated as an "Unordered Topic".
requirements.condition: For every Topic without an explicit unordered override
requirements.required_behavior: Treat it as an Ordered Topic by default.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not default a Topic to unordered behavior.
requirements.why_checkable: A newly used Topic's delivery behavior can be tested before configuration.

requirements.quote:
[MQTT-4.6.0-5]	A Server MUST by default treat each Topic as an "Ordered Topic".
It MAY provide an administrative or other mechanism to allow one or more Topics to be treated as an "Unordered Topic".
requirements.condition: For one or more Topics
requirements.required_behavior: The Server is permitted to provide a mechanism that marks them Unordered.
requirements.why_checkable: MAY makes the override mechanism optional and imposes no mandatory implementation choice.
